name: Willard Richards
role: Apostle, Church historian, and survivor of Carthage Jail
dateNote: He was called as an apostle by section 118 in July 1838 and ordained in England on 14 April 1840.
importance: Section 118 names him to fill a vacancy in the Twelve while he was serving in England. He became Joseph Smith’s secretary and Church historian in 1842 and recorded his teachings. His records lie behind sections 110, 126, 129, and 130. Section 135 says he and John Taylor were the only others in the Carthage jail room in 1844, and he escaped unhurt.
connections: Baptized by Brigham Young and later Young’s counselor in the First Presidency. He married Jennetta Richards in England in 1838.
reviewNote: Birth, baptism (31 December 1836 by Brigham Young), England mission, apostle ordination, historian and recorder roles, Carthage, and later offices checked on JSP; death 11 March 1854 shown in a fragment.
